title: Ineffectiveness of KeraVio Treatment with Violet Light-Emitting Glasses Without Riboflavin Drops for Progressive Keratoconus

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) license)

groups.description: Randomized control group of a double-masked trial: one eye per patient with keratoconus progressing within 6 months before baseline, wearing pseudo-placebo glasses with minimal violet light irradiance (< 0.01 mW/cm2) for 6 months; no cross-linking (Methods 2.2, Table 1)

series.notes: mean ± SD; Kmax from anterior segment OCT (CASIA, Tomey); all 8 eyes followed to 6 months (Results 3.1)

exclusions.reason: violet light without riboflavin is neither cross-linking nor a ring segment and the group is not an untreated observation group: out of scope

exclusions.what: PMC11818551.xml::jcm-14-00773-t002 column C6 (Change from Baseline to 6 Months)
exclusions.reason: change column; the absolute series of the same group is used
fellow eyes not declared as an observation group; not tabulated

notes: The control group wore identical frames emitting minimal violet light (< 0.01 mW/cm2; 29.2 J/cm2 over 6 months) to keep the masking; classified as a sham observation group.
Age group unstated: inclusion allowed patients aged 7 years or older and only the group mean ± SD of age is reported (Table 1).
Randomization 2:1 (trial to control); the more severely affected eye was treated when both eyes qualified.
Thinnest corneal thickness (Table 2), visual acuity and refraction (Table 3) are tabulated and not used.
